chapter.name: Exploring Algebraic Identities
chapter.blurb: Identities for squares and cubes, factorisation, algebra tiles, and simplifying rational expressions.

scope_in.item: Identity versus equation; (a + b)^2 and (a - b)^2 with geometric models; expanding and squaring numbers
Factorise perfect-square expressions, taking out a common factor first
(a + b + c)^2 and a^2 - b^2 = (a + b)(a - b); squaring numbers with Sridharacharya's method

Cubic identities (a + b)^3, (a - b)^3, x^3 - y^3, x^3 + y^3 and x^3 + y^3 + z^3 - 3xyz and their uses
Simplify rational expressions by factorising and cancelling non-zero common factors; area and volume applications

concepts.name: Identities and the squares (a + b)^2 and (a - b)^2
concepts.description: The difference between an equation and an identity, the identities for (a + b)^2 and (a - b)^2, their geometric models and use in squaring expressions and numbers.
concepts.idea: An identity is true for every value of its variables; (a + b)^2 has the extra middle term 2ab that a^2 + b^2 lacks.
concepts.rule: (a + b)^2 = a^2 + 2ab + b^2 and (a - b)^2 = a^2 - 2ab + b^2, true for all numbers a and b.

concepts.name: Factorising quadratics: x^2 + (a + b)x + ab and algebra tiles
concepts.description: Products of two linear expressions, splitting the middle term, factorising quadratics and the general product (px + a)(qx + b).
concepts.idea: A quadratic x^2 + sx + t factorises when two numbers a and b have sum s and product t.
concepts.rule: (x + a)(x + b) = x^2 + (a + b)x + ab. To factorise, find a and b with a + b equal to the x-coefficient and ab equal to the constant. (px + a)(qx + b) = pqx^2 + (pb + aq)x + ab.
concepts.example: x^2 + 11x + 30: a + b = 11 and ab = 30 give 5 and 6, so (x + 5)(x + 6).

concepts.name: Simplifying rational expressions and applications
concepts.description: Cancelling common factors of the numerator and denominator after factorising, and using factorisation for areas and volumes.
concepts.idea: A rational expression is simplified by factorising top and bottom and cancelling a common factor that is not zero.
concepts.rule: Factorise numerator and denominator (common factor, identities, a + b and ab method), cancel common non-zero factors. The value of a factor must not be zero for cancelling.
